- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) and forecast is high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) and forecast is low, raise forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent price history shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast peak and smooth decline.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true outcome by 2–3% in early days of 30d horizon, apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to early forecast points.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment spikes, model tends to lag — forecast should be slightly ahead of true trend in early horizon.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome in late horizon (e.g., last 5–7 days), apply a small upward bias to compensate for mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), avoid extreme forecast swings — use smoother transition between highs and lows.
